What's the difference between mise/unuse, mise/uninstall, and mise/cache/clear?

Pick one: stop using a tool in this config → mise unuse; keep config but drop binaries → mise uninstall; fix stale downloads or cache corruption → mise cache clear. See also mise/Q/How do I remove a mise tool?.

Will calling mise/upgrade in a directory that has a local upgrade global mise/Tools?
Short answer: Yes. mise upgrade without flags operates on the merged config stack, so global tools are upgraded regardless of whether the CWD has a local mise.toml.
Will calling mise/upgrade in a directory that has a local upgrade global mise/Tools?
Will calling mise/upgrade in a directory that has a local upgrade global mise/Tools?

mise merges all config sources in order (global ~/.config/mise/config.toml, then local .mise.toml / mise.toml, etc.). Running mise upgrade resolves tools from that full merged config, which includes tools defined only in global config.
Will calling mise/upgrade in a directory that has a local upgrade global mise/Tools?
To restrict upgrades to the project-local config only — skipping tools that appear exclusively in global config — pass --local (see src/cli/upgrade.rs).
Will calling mise/upgrade in a directory that has a local upgrade global mise/Tools?
To target only globally-configured tools, run mise upgrade from a directory that has no local mise.toml (e.g. ~), or name the tools explicitly: mise upgrade <tool>.

What Is a Shim in mise? Shims | mise-en-place

A shim is a tiny executable that masquerades as the tool you want to run (e.g. node, prettier). Each shim is a symlink to the mise binary that intercepts your shell call, figures out which version of the tool should run, loads the declared mise/Environment changes, and then delegates execution. See Shims in the mise docs.

mise/activate rewrites on every prompt; this is great for interactive shells but unavailable to non-interactive environments like CI, IDEs, or scripts. Shims offer a static directory of stand-ins that works even when the shell cannot evaluate mise activate. See Shims vs PATH activation.

By default, shims live in ~/.local/share/mise/shims. Adding this directory to PATH (or using mise activate --shims) makes every installed tool appear globally available. See mise activate --shims.

[tools] pins a versioned binary and gives you a mise/Shim; tasks merely use whatever is already on PATH.

Mise can be used to install and run tools, launch tasks, and manage environment variables. Choosing where a command lives decides whether it is upgraded by mise or by the command's own update mechanism.
New users often add every CLI to [tools], then wonder why npx prettier or pipx some-app discovers a newer version than prettier --version run directly.
The clash is most visible with Node CLIs such as Claude Code: a shimmed claude froze at 0.2.115 while npx @anthropic-ai/claude-code updated to 1.0.11.
Pin runtimes & long-lived CLIs. Anything you expect teammates or CI to call directly (python, terraform, aws_okta_keyman) belongs in [tools]. See Dev Tools Overview.
On-demand wrappers stay in tasks. Commands that bootstrap themselves each run (npx, go run, cargo install --locked) should be invoked inside the run = "..." line. See Tasks Guide.
One source of truth. A given binary should be provided either by a shim or by its own downloader—never both.
Shims & activation. When a tool lives in [tools], mise installs it and places a shim earlier in PATH. Running prettier or aws_okta_keyman now hits that shim. See How it works.
exec / run. Tasks inherit the full "mise context" (all shims & env-vars) via mise run or mise exec.
The docs even show mixing backends:
Runtime: node = "lts" → shimmed node; tasks can just say node script.js.
Project tool: ruff = "latest" ensures the same linter version everywhere.
One-shot generator: keep cookiecutter out of [tools] and call it via npx or pipx run.
"npx will respect my [tools] pin." Not true; npx downloads a fresh copy into its own cache, bypassing shims. See npx and mise.
"pipx: entries auto-update on every run." They install once; updates come from mise up or version bumps.
"Tasks require the tool in [tools]. Tasks can run any shell command; [tools] is only needed if that command expects the shim.
